title: MCP is all you need — Samuel Colvin, Pydantic
talk_summary: Samuel Colvin argues MCP's tool-calling primitive (plus sampling, logging, and stdio subprocess transport) is enough to compose agents and tools without bespoke agent-to-agent protocols. The key practical pattern: push inference and heavy context into an MCP tool server so the main agent's context stays small, and use MCP sampling so tool servers borrow the client's LLM instead of configuring their own.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of shipping SQL instructions/schema into the main agent's tool description, they run a separate inner agent inside the MCP tool server that generates and validates the query, returning only the result to the outer agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: doing this kind of thing where we're doing the inference inside a tool is a powerful way of effectively limiting uh the context window of the of the main running agent

takeaways.technique: MCP sampling: tool server borrows the client's LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP server that needs an LLM sends a sampling request back through the client, which proxies it to its configured model and returns the response, so sub-tools don't need their own model credentials or quota.

takeaways.technique: Streaming progress logs from long tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Tool servers emit context.log/progress messages back to the client while the tool is still executing, giving visibility into multi-minute operations before completion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can give these logs while the tool call is still executing

takeaways.what_they_do: They strip markdown fences, check the table name, run the query, and on failure raise a model-retry so the LLM is re-prompted with the error instead of failing the run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the query fails we're going to uh raise model retry with impantic to go and retry

takeaways.technique: Stdio subprocess MCP servers for isolation
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP servers run as subprocesses over stdin/stdout, giving process isolation and simple lifecycle management versus HTTP services.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP's way of being allowed to operate as effectively a subprocess over standard in and standard out is extremely useful

takeaways.technique: Avoid bespoke agent-to-agent protocols; compose via MCP tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agents-as-tools over MCP is sufficient and people over-engineer new A2A communication schemes; tools and agents compose without knowing each other.
takeaways.evidence_quote: people are over complicating the situation sometimes trying to come up with new ways of doing agentto agent communication
